subject: Pilot acceptance plan & scoring matrix — Horizon Health
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot acceptance plan & scoring matrix — Horizon Health

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Short recap and a proposed plan to get the pilot (pilot = short production-facing evaluation) moving so we can validate both quality and performance before a larger rollout. Please confirm owners and any adjustments to the acceptance criteria below.

High-level approach (two lanes):
- Phase A: Offline assessment (sanitized sample datasets) — objective scoring against a lightweight rubric to validate basic quality and hallucination profile.
- Phase B: Live shadow run (non-incident traffic routed to Redwood for scoring in parallel) — measure latency, throughput, and end-to-end behavior; final acceptance decision uses both lanes.

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Accuracy/Relevance: weighted score >= 0.78 (weights: relevance 50%, hallucination 20%, precision 15%, human-review pass-rate 15%)
- Hallucination rate: < 6% on the labeled sample set
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 350 ms (with target token lengths per your call: median ~60 tokens)
- Throughput: sustain 200 rps for the expected shadow traffic profile
- Integration: SDK + UI embed within 2 s of API response (non-blocking)

Scoring matrix and attached acceptance spreadsheet (horizon-acceptance-matrix.xlsx) includes per-category definitions, sample labeling guidance, and passing thresholds.

Data & security notes:
- For Phase A please provide a sanitized sample (3 datasets: 250–1,000 rows each). We can sign an NDA and accept S3 transfer or secure upload.
- For Phase B shadowing, we'll use production-mirroring only — no writes — and keep logs in your VPC if you prefer.

Proposed timeline (draft):
- Jul 26: Data share (sanitized samples)
- Jul 27–29: Offline runs + scoring
- Jul 30: Review session to go over scores + adjust thresholds if needed
- Aug 2–15: Shadow run in-parallel (2 weeks)
- Aug 17: Final acceptance decision and next steps

Owners / next steps (please confirm):
- Horizon technical lead: Tom Ellis (to deliver datasets and access)
- Redwood SE: Marissa Cole (runs offline scoring, coordinates shadow)
- Redwood AM: Diego Fernandez (commercials, timeline owner)

Attachments: pilot-sow-draft.pdf (draft SOW), horizon-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (scoring matrix)

If this looks good, I’ll send a calendar invite for the Jul 30 review and open the S3 upload link once we have the go-ahead.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Diego — this is helpful and a good starting point. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Compliance / PII: We need confirmation that any sample data will be handled under our DPA and that logs for the shadow run can be kept within our environment (we prefer AWS KMS + customer-managed keys). Please have your security contact outline the flow.

2) Evaluation metric preference: Our clinical reviewers prefer a recall-weighted metric for the first pass (we care more about missing critical content than a slight drop in precision). Can you accommodate a weighted-recall variant in the scoring matrix?

3) Human review: For the offline assessment, we’ll do a human-in-the-loop labeling pass (3 clinical SMEs) — can Redwood accept labeled gold sets and run automated scoring against that?

4) Sample datasets: attaching the filenames we propose to share (sample-dataset-1.csv, sample-dataset-2.csv). We’ll confirm exact rows after our internal scrub.

Tom will act as our technical lead and will work directly with Marissa on upload details.

We’re leaning to start with Phase A only initially — happy to expand to shadowing once offline numbers look good.

—Priya
Director of Product, Horizon Health
Attachments: sample-dataset-1.csv (stub), sample-dataset-2.csv (stub)

Hi Priya / Tom —

Happy to take point on the technical assessment. Quick response to the asks above and an updated operational plan (details below).

Security / data handling
- We can support AWS KMS with customer-managed keys for any artifacts we store. For the offline run, if you prefer, we’ll perform the scoring in your account via a temporary role (Redwood SE-run job). I’ll follow up with our security checklist and an anonymization checklist.

Scoring matrix (proposed adjustments per your recall preference)
- New weighted categories with sample weights: recall-weighted relevance 55%, hallucination 15%, latency 10%, robustness/edge-case failure 10%, human-review divergence 10%.
- Pass threshold: composite >= 0.75 (we can tune after the first offline batch).
- Sample size: recommend 2,000 labeled rows for a statistically meaningful signal; minimum viable test: 500 rows.
- Labeling instructions: we’ll provide a short rubric for SME labeling (attached within the acceptance matrix).

Offline evaluation steps (Phase A)
1) Horizon shares sanitized sample(s) (expected Jul 26)
2) Redwood runs two model variants against the set (baseline + tuned) Jul 27–29
3) Marissa runs automated scoring and produces a CSV with per-row flags + summary metrics (Deliverable: offline-scoring-summary.csv)
4) Review call Jul 30 to discuss results and next steps

Shadow run (Phase B) — optional, only if Phase A meets threshold
- Run length: 2 weeks recommended, minimum 5 business days
- Observables: p50/p95 latency, per-request cost, tail error rates, token distribution, and a sample of human-reviewed outputs for regression checks

Ownership and communication
- Technical delivery: Marissa Cole (marissa@redwood.com)
- Commercial & timeline: Diego Fernandez (diego@redwood.com)
- Escalation (contracts/security): Vivek Kulkarni (vivek@redwood.com)

I’ll upload the detailed rubric and a small script to normalize CSV columns into the Drive folder and share the secure upload instructions after we sign the minimal DPA.

Attachments/links referenced: horizon-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (updated with recall-weighted variant), internal-drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3horizon-pilot

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
